playbook.step: Pick a niche with data, not vibes
playbook.detail: Check tag-level supply growth and success rates before choosing. Cozy overall: 11% of 2024-H1'25 releases hit 1,000 reviews (2.6x Steam) but releases grew +143% in 2026 vs Steam +45%. Avoid fastest-filling niches (Shop Keeper +634%, Idler +150%) unless you have a sharp twist; favor slow-filling high-odds niches (Survival Craft 28.3%, +39%).
playbook.benchmark: 1,000 reviews ~= $150k gross; Steam baseline 4.2% of games reach it

playbook.step: Treat 'cozy' as a mood layer on a real genre
playbook.detail: Steam Page Analyzer: 'Cozy' is a mood tag layered on top of a genre and overlaps farming, life sim and puzzle. Define the genre hook first, the cozy tone second.
GameDiscoverCo found 'cozy' used as a primary descriptor by 3.1% of $100k+ Steam games in 2025 vs 0.4% in 2022 (+675%) - a label the audience reacts positively to.

playbook.step: Steam page live early; build to 2k wishlists before Next Fest
playbook.detail: HTMAG Next Fest survey data: games see no meaningful Next Fest lift below ~2,000 pre-fest wishlists; Gold tier = 7,000-9,999 wishlists earned in-fest.
playbook.benchmark: 2,000+ wishlists pre-Next Fest; 7,000 wishlists ~= Popular Upcoming at launch

playbook.step: Use wishlist velocity as a go/no-go signal
playbook.detail: VG Insights: wishlist momentum is a strong success indicator, but mainly for games reaching 100k+ wishlists pre-launch; action/adventure out-wishlists other genres, so cozy games should benchmark against cozy peers.

Case study of a farming-adjacent game reaching 220,000 wishlists in 3 months (How To Market A Game). No session-verified, cozy-specific TikTok benchmark was found; test GIF/short-video hooks and track wishlist conversion per post.
Enter Next Fest once the demo is polished and you already have 2k+ wishlists; Feb 2025 fest had 2,244 participating games (HTMAG survey n=208).

playbook.step: Cozy showcases: Wholesome Direct, Day of the Devs and cozy-specific festivals
playbook.detail: [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Wholesome Direct (June, Summer Game Fest window) is the flagship cozy showcase; Day of the Devs is a curated indie showcase. Apply 6+ months ahead and line up a Steam page/demo for the traffic spike. No session-verified wishlist-per-showcase benchmarks were found.

GameDiscoverCo: post-Lethal Company, devs realized virality compounds with online co-op; co-op keywords up 1.4% -> 2.1% (2023-2025). Bongo Cat's friends-on-desktop feature coincided with continued player growth.
Across cozy niches, sub-$5 titles almost never reach 1,000 reviews while $20+ titles do far better (correlation also reflects production value).
playbook.benchmark: Cozy: <$5 2.7% vs $20+ 45.2%; Farming 1.7% vs 24.4%; Life sim 2% vs 34.2%; City builder $20+ 46.5%; Idler best at $10-14.99 (16.1%); Roguelike DB best at $15-19.99 (22.7%)

playbook.step: Early Access can work for systemic cozy games
playbook.detail: Fields of Mistria: 100k downloads in EA week 1, 250k in month 1, 98% positive on 2,400+ reviews; 1.0 in Aug 2026 after ~2 years of EA, reportedly passing 1M copies around 1.0, then console ports announced.

playbook.step: Ship PC-native UX even if you plan mobile
playbook.detail: Heartopia's Steam launch was ~66% positive mainly due to mobile-first UI and missing controller support, despite huge CCU.

playbook.step: Steady content updates through Early Access
playbook.detail: Fields of Mistria kept an Early Access roadmap of major updates to 1.0 while holding ~98% positive. [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Cozy EA titles typically ship a major content update every ~2-4 months; no session-verified cadence benchmark was gathered.

playbook.step: Don't over-build live service before product-market fit
playbook.detail: Singularity 6 raised ~$49M for Palia, then cut staff in three rounds (Sept 2023-May 2024) and sold to Daybreak in July 2024 despite millions of players.
Fields of Mistria announced Switch/PS5/Xbox after its PC 1.0; Palia expanded to PS5/Xbox with the Elderwood expansion.
Grow a Garden (cozy gardening) peaked ~22M CCU; Roblox paid >$1.5B to creators in 2025. A small Roblox spin-off can test a cozy loop cheaply or extend a brand.

[PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Follow Steam's discount cooldown rules and regional pricing recommendations; join seasonal sales once launch velocity fades.

funding.typicalTerms: Keep 100% IP and revenue (minus platform fee); EA revenue funds the rest of development.
funding.prosCons: Pro: full control; Fields of Mistria shows EA can fund a cozy game to 1.0 (100k week-1 downloads). Con: needs a playable, compelling EA build and personal runway.

funding.typicalTerms: [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Publisher advances development + marketing budget, recoups first, then splits net revenue; commonly cited splits range from 50/50 to 70/30 in the developer's favor after recoup, with IP usually staying with the developer for indie deals.
funding.prosCons: Pro: funding, marketing, ports, localization, QA. Con: recoupment can delay dev revenue; terms vary widely - get a lawyer. (No session-verified 2025-26 term survey gathered.)

funding.typicalTerms: Equity in exchange for capital sized for live-service growth.
funding.prosCons: Con example: Singularity 6 raised ~$49M for cozy MMO Palia, then had three rounds of layoffs and was acquired by Daybreak. VC scale pushes toward live-service scope a small cozy team rarely needs.

funding.typicalTerms: [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Non-dilutive; Epic MegaGrants awards range from about $5k to $500k for Unreal projects; national programs (e.g. Canada Media Fund, UK Games Fund, Creative Europe) vary by country and often require matching funds.
funding.prosCons: Pro: no equity/recoup. Con: competitive, slow, eligibility constraints.

funding.typicalTerms: [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Backers pre-buy; platform fee ~5% plus payment processing. Cozy example: Coral Island raised roughly $1.6M on Kickstarter in 2021.
funding.prosCons: Pro: validates demand, builds community. Con: needs an existing audience and polished pitch; fulfillment obligations. No session-verified 2024-26 cozy Kickstarter benchmarks were gathered.

funding.option: Platform deals (Netflix, Apple Arcade, subscription services)
funding.typicalTerms: [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Upfront fee/minimum guarantee for exclusivity or catalog inclusion; terms are private.
funding.prosCons: Pro: de-risks budget. Con: exclusivity limits Steam upside. Netflix is investing in cozy (Spirit Crossing cozy MMO).

funding.typicalTerms: Revenue via Robux converted through Developer Exchange; Roblox paid >$1.5B to creators in 2025; top 1,000 creators averaged ~$0.8-1M.
funding.prosCons: Pro: zero distribution cost, huge audience. Con: young audience, monetization design, extreme hit concentration.

localization.whyItMatters: [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Simplified Chinese is consistently one of the top two languages in the Steam Hardware & Software Survey. Session evidence: Chinese studio XD's cozy life sim Heartopia peaked at 66k Steam CCU, showing a large Chinese-speaking cozy audience and competition.

Japanese press covers Western cozy hits (e.g. Denfaminicogamer on Webfishing). [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Japan is a strong Switch market, relevant for console ports of cozy games.
German outlets (PC Games Hardware, GamePro, Mein-MMO) regularly cover the cozy trend and cozy releases (Rusty's Retirement, Fields of Mistria ports), indicating an engaged cozy audience.
Taiwanese outlet 4Gamers published a cozy-games Steam trend analysis in 2026; cheap incremental add once Simplified Chinese exists.
Russian outlets reported on cozy/single-player growth on Steam in 2026. [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Russian is a top-5 Steam language.

French (Gameblog on Fields of Mistria 1.0) and Italian (Multiplayer.it on cozy growth) press cover the trend. [PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese are large Steam languages; Steamworks recommends localizing store pages at minimum.
[PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-verified in this research session; confirm before relying on it] Common top-10 Steam language; often bundled with CJK localization pass.

budgets.note: Rule of thumb from Steam Page Analyzer. Steam takes a platform fee and refunds/VAT/regional pricing reduce net, so net is materially below gross. A game needs well above 1,000 reviews to repay a multi-person, multi-year budget.

DERIVED ARITHMETIC, not a sourced survey: 2-4 people x 18 months x ~$4k-$10k fully loaded monthly cost per person (varies hugely by country), plus ~10-20% for audio, localization, QA and marketing. Cozy $20+ titles reach 1,000 reviews 45.2% of the time vs 2.7% under $5, so price for the budget.

budgets.scope: Solo/duo idle or desktop companion, 3-6 months
budgets.note: DERIVED ARITHMETIC: 1-2 people x 3-6 months x ~$4k-$5k/month. Only 5.6% of idlers reach 1,000 reviews and 54 can ship in a single week, so keep it cheap; best price band $10-14.99.
DERIVED ARITHMETIC: 4-8 people x 24-30 months x ~$6k-$10k/month plus netcode/QA overhead. Highest-odds niche (28.3% to 1,000 reviews) justifies larger scope, often with publisher funding.
Not a first-project scope; Palia's developer still needed layoffs and a sale despite millions of players.

failureModes.mode: Launching a generic farming/life sim into the flood
failureModes.detail: Farming sim: 1,198 unreleased pages queued; life sim: 3,074. Players and press voice fatigue with farming sims.
Under-$5 cozy titles reach 1,000 reviews only 2.7% of the time (farming 1.7%, life sim 2%, creature collector 1.8%) vs 24-46% for $20+ in the same niches.

failureModes.mode: Too few wishlists before Next Fest
failureModes.detail: HTMAG data: no meaningful Next Fest lift below ~2,000 pre-fest wishlists; 7,000 is roughly the Popular Upcoming threshold.
Shop Keeper releases went from 65 to 477 in the same weeks year-on-year (+634%); Idler +150%; past success rates were earned before the flood.
PC Gamer: 54 idle games in one week, many 'eerily similar'; visual sameness makes discoverability nearly impossible.

failureModes.mode: Over-scoped live service funded by VC
failureModes.detail: Palia's developer raised ~$49M, then three layoff rounds and acquisition by Daybreak (July 2024).
Heartopia's Steam reception (~66%) was dragged down by lack of controller support and PC optimization.
Cozy is a mood tag over a genre; games need a clear genre hook. Creature collectors (in Pokemon's shadow) show the weakest odds of measured niches (5.9%).
